pid_data.process_description: Process Overview The highlighted section of the P&ID represents the VCM charging and transfer system that primarily delivers Vinyl Chloride Monomer (VCM) from the fresh VCM storage tanks SV-101A/B to the polymerization reactor SR-301 through the red-line flow path. In addition to the fresh VCM supply, the system interfaces with the recovered VCM storage tanks SV-111A/B, which serve as an alternate or recovery source within the overall VCM handling system. However, SV-111A/B are not part of the red-line highlighted transfer route. The active charging path includes SV-101A/B, transfer pumps SP-101A/B, filters SF-101A/B and SF-107A/B, and the associated piping, valves, and instrumentation required to ensure controlled and safe VCM charging into the reactor. Process Initiation Under normal operation, the process initiates with liquid VCM withdrawn from the fresh VCM storage tanks SV-101A/B by starting one of the transfer pumps SP-101A/B after opening the appropriate outlet isolation valves. The recovered VCM tanks SV-111A/B remain isolated during this operation and are maintained as standby or recovery inventory. If operational conditions require the use of recovered VCM, SV-111A/B can be aligned through dedicated connections; however, this alignment does not utilize the red-line flow path shown on the P&ID. Initial filtration and instrumentation verify that pressure, flow, and temperature are within acceptable limits before downstream transfer continues. Process End The process concludes when the required quantity of VCM is delivered into reactor SR-301 through the designated feed connection. After completion of the charging operation, the transfer pumps are stopped and the relevant isolation valves are closed to secure the system and prevent unintended VCM movement prior to the reaction phase. Process Description Liquid VCM drawn from SV-101A/B is pressurized by the transfer pumps SP-101A/B and routed through the red-line piping network. The stream passes through filters SF-101A/B and SF-107A/B to remove particulates and ensure feed quality, followed by isolation valves for operational control, check valves to prevent reverse flow, and instrumented sections for continuous monitoring of process conditions. The recovered VCM tanks SV-111A/B are connected to the system for inventory management and recovery purposes but remain hydraulically separated from the red-line charging route during normal operation. The conditioned VCM stream then proceeds through the charging line toward the reactor feed header, maintaining controlled pressure and temperature up to the reactor inlet. File Description The P&ID file (Red-Line and Red-circle Detection Scope) – documents the piping and instrumentation configuration for the fresh VCM charging operation. For detection and analysis purposes, only the red-line highlighted flow path is considered, covering SV-101A/B, SP-101A/B, SF-101A/B, SF-107A/B, associated piping, valves, instrumentation, and the reactor feed interface to SR-301. Recovered VCM systems, including SV-111A/B, as well as non-highlighted utilities, are outside the scope of this description.
